title: Steelers Bench Multiple Starters for Eagles Clash, More Roster Tweaks Expected – Steelers Depot
body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers entered the final stretch of the 2024 season with a visibly altered roster, benching a slew of veterans ahead of the showdown with the Philadelphia Eagles and signaling that further personnel shifts are on the horizon. Head coach Mike McCarthy, still reeling from back‑to‑back defeats – a 27‑10 loss to the Eagles and a 31‑17 setback against the Cincinnati Bengals the week before – told the media that “the status quo isn’t working,” and promised a decisive overhaul to spark a turnaround before the playoffs become a distant dream.

The most immediate change came before the Eagles game, when the Steelers announced a revised depth chart that saw starting safety Jordan Whitehead, veteran linebacker Devin Bush, and wide receiver Diontae Johnson relegated to the bench. In their stead, younger players such as safety Cameron Sutton, linebacker Kenny Pickett (who also serves as the quarterback), and rookie receiver Jalin Hyatt were promoted to starting roles. The move was not merely cosmetic; it reflected McCarthy’s growing impatience with a unit that has struggled to protect the quarterback, generate consistent offensive rhythm, and stop opposing pass rushes. “We have to put the ball in the hands of players who are hungry, who are playing with a chip on their shoulder,” McCarthy said during the pre‑game press conference.

Analysts point out that the Steelers’ defensive rankings have slipped into the bottom third of the league, with a points‑allowed average of 27.3 per game, a stark contrast to the stout, top‑ten defense that defined the franchise in the early 2020s. The benching of Whitehead, who has been a reliable tackler but has shown lapses in coverage against speedy receivers, underscores a shift toward more aggressive, ball‑hawking schemes. Sutton, who posted 1.5 sacks and three forced fumbles in limited action last season, is expected to bring a blitz‑heavy approach that could disrupt the Eagles’ prolific passing attack led by Jalen Hurts.

On offense, the decision to sideline Diontae Johnson—who amassed over 1,000 receiving yards last year—signals a willingness to gamble on untested talent in a unit that has sputtered at critical moments. The Steelers have struggled to convert third‑down opportunities, ranking 28th in conversion rate, and have been plagued by an inconsistent running game that averages just 3.9 yards per carry. Hyatt, a second‑round pick from the University of Texas, has shown flashes of speed and route‑running precision in preseason, and McCarthy hopes his injection of fresh legs will stretch the Eagles’ secondary and open up space for the ground attack.

The ripple effects of these changes extend beyond the immediate matchup. The Steelers’ front office, led by General Manager Omar Khan, is reportedly reviewing the entire roster, with a particular focus on the offensive line, where injuries have left the unit shorthanded and vulnerable. Veteran guard Kevin Dotson and tackle Isaiah Wilson have both been listed as questionable, and the team may look to the practice squad or free‑agency market to plug gaps before the season’s final two games. Moreover, the benchings have sent a clear message to the locker room: performance will be the sole criterion for playing time, regardless of tenure.

While the adjustments are bold, they come with risk. Young players thrust into starting roles may struggle against the Eagles’ high‑powered offense, potentially widening the scoring gap. Yet the Steelers’ recent 0‑2 record against AFC East opponents has left the franchise with little to lose and everything to gain. If the revamped lineup can at least keep the game within reach, it could restore confidence and buy McCarthy the breathing room needed to fine‑tune his schemes for the season’s concluding stretch.

Looking ahead, Pittsburgh faces a crucial test not only against Philadelphia but also in the upcoming contests with the Cleveland Browns and the Baltimore Ravens. The success of the benchings and any subsequent roster moves will likely dictate whether the Steelers can salvage a playoff berth or settle for a rebuilding year. As the team recalibrates its strategy, fans and pundits alike will be watching closely to see if McCarthy’s promised changes translate into tangible improvement on the field.
